Cohora, an eight-page team workspace for a film studio in powder blue with a black icon rail, where task statistics switch between the week and the month, the next meeting is dismissed with Undo, cuts are reviewed with timecoded notes and a review stage, and the trends morph between focus, reach and tasks, with a call room, files and an Appearance panel that restyles it live; Curava, a ten-page patient-care app in navy and seafoam with a curved rail whose bubble travels from page to page, where a visit is booked in four steps with Undo, the heart-rate chart morphs between 7, 30 and 90 days and today's medicines tick off, with vitals and lab results, a pharmacy with checkout, video visits, an inbox and an Appearance panel that restyles it live; Carevo, a six-page patient health dashboard in forest and lime with a booking column on every page, where a doctor is booked on a calendar of free, full and off days, the heart rate flows as a live wave, a weight dial is dragged to log today and the vitals morph between 7 days and a year, with medicines and refill warnings, lab results on their ranges and an Appearance panel that restyles it live; Radiva, an eight-page patient imaging-results portal in mint and charcoal with a nav capsule whose light disc hangs from the active page, where the radiologist's note is read in plain words, two scans are compared by dragging a divider across them, a scan is booked at a nearby imaging centre in four steps and the visit's prep checklist is ticked off, with sharing by doctor, a body guide, a glossary, a care chat and an Appearance panel that restyles it live; and Terrova, a seven-page renewable-energy operations dashboard in sage, lime and charcoal, where the week's production rides on lollipops that morph between weeks, an air-quality map glides between regions, jobs move lane by lane on a maintenance board and an invoice is stamped paid, with battery banks, grid trading, carbon credits and an Appearance panel that restyles it live. Each has calm, transform-only motion, ready to wire to your own data.

collections.name: Login & sign-up forms
collections.tagline: Sign-in screens with a character — pandas, cats, glass and light.
collections.intro: Sign-in and sign-up forms people remember: a panda that covers its eyes for your password, a cat that peeks, liquid glass, a door that opens, a password that hatches a guardian. Each is plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript you can drop into any project.

collections.name: Shop templates
collections.tagline: Whole online shops — catalogue, product, bag and checkout, ready for your brand.
collections.intro: Complete storefronts you can rebrand and launch: SOLUM, a nine-page trail-apparel store with a scroll-played hero film, a full checkout and an admin panel, in TypeScript; Fitlo, a clothing and shoe shop whose product pages carry a three-step size advisor, with its own admin dashboard one switch away, in React and TypeScript; Rayé, a striped-shirt store whose home page plays like an ad film, with a height-and-weight size finder, a bag drawer and a working checkout, in React and TypeScript; Glint, a streetwear store whose pinned hero weaves a giant wordmark through the model, with a lookbook that adds whole looks, showroom fitting bookings and a working checkout, in React and TypeScript; Kesten, a menswear tailor's store whose giant wordmark rises behind three men, with a size guide, a four-step fitting booker and a working checkout, in React and TypeScript; Lunde Studio, a solid-wood furniture store whose hero holds over a sunlit room film and whose craft film walks through four workshop steps as you scroll, with mega menus, filters, finishes and a working checkout, in React and TypeScript; KVIST, a bento-grid home-goods store with sign-in and a live admin dashboard, in React, Tailwind and Firebase; Kessler, a six-page leather-goods shop on a modernist grid; Norda, a one-page Nordic home-goods store that moves like a film; Sorrel, a botanical skincare shop where every bottle tosses itself into the bag; Sola, a footwear atelier whose cart is a real shopping bag; Oria, a furniture store with a scroll-film home page, a filterable shop, product pages, a bag and a working checkout, in TypeScript; and Camber, a performance-parts store whose hero swaps between five vehicles and whose build film plays as you scroll. Kessler, Norda, Sorrel, Sola and Camber are plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript.

collections.name: Business dashboards
collections.tagline: Run the company — sales, projects, people, stock, the till and customer messages.
collections.intro: Eighty-five dashboards for running a business: Halden, a six-page sales CRM with a drag-and-drop pipeline; Tandem, a sales workspace where you work a ranked lead queue and every lead score explains itself; Fernly for projects across seven pages; Coterie for people ops and hiring; Grovia, the same in mint-green glass; Wharf for stock and orders; Ledge, a shop's point of sale, stock and purchase orders, where a sale flies into the ticket and prints its receipt; Parley, a two-way inbox for customer messages with campaigns, automations and reports; Rapport, an eight-page sales CRM where a deal takes its stage’s colour as you drag it and every customer has a profile of their deals, tasks and details; Sprig, a twelve-page studio CRM where a deal is dragged into Won, with companies, contacts, meetings, email and a report builder; Mender, a support-desk CRM where cases drag between lanes and you assign each case’s steps by dragging people onto them; Accord, an eight-page client-pipeline CRM whose deal cards lean as you drag them between stages and open dark to show the contact; Tend, a seven-page clinic CRM with a WhatsApp inbox, patient records, a clinician schedule and reminder broadcasts; Corbel, a thirteen-page sales dashboard for a shop that sells online and in store, with products, orders, customers, an inbox, email campaigns, automations and analytics; Lintel, a real-estate CRM where you set a listing's price on a gauge with two sliders, with homes for sale and to rent, a deal board that stamps SOLD, scored leads and a live chat; Hearth, a twelve-page mortgage CRM for loan officers, with leads, loan files, a document vault and a pipeline where a funded loan floats its commission up; Torque, an eight-page admin panel for a car repair workshop, with a live floor of bays and lifts, a job board, repair orders with a digital inspection and customer-approved estimates, a bay planner, parts and invoices; Pane, a seven-page team workspace in liquid glass, with home widgets and activity rings, a focus timer that runs in a capsule at the top, a drag-and-drop task board, a calendar, projects and insights; Ivora, a fifteen-page dental practice app with live chairs, an interactive tooth chart, a chair planner, treatment plans, prescriptions, lab cases and insurance claims; Cadra, an ERP for a bike maker with a drag-and-drop Gantt production schedule, work orders, a sales board, a showroom till, purchasing, three warehouses, shipments, people and payroll, a ledger and invoices; Tavola, a nine-page restaurant operations dashboard in glassmorphism, with a kitchen board you drag tickets across, a floor plan you seat guests on, bookings, menu engineering, stock, a staff rota and sales reports; Lumora, a seventeen-section teacher's dashboard for a school, with a day ribbon, registers, a drag-and-drop seating plan, a timetable, lesson plans, a marking queue, an AI quiz builder and a gradebook; Sunrow, a sixteen-section field ERP for a solar and battery-storage builder, with a drag-and-drop Gantt schedule, projects, contractors, materials and purchase orders, budgets, approvals, timesheets, safety and equipment; Vessa, a nine-section inventory app for a skincare lab, with stock across three locations, production batches with QA release and expiry, a pick-pack-ship order board, purchasing, bin maps and analytics; Noria, an eight-page workflow-automation app for a freight forwarder's ops desk, with a live run pulse, a node-canvas flow builder with test runs and failures grouped by cause; Mavora, an eight-page store dashboard for a coffee roaster, with takings by channel against a daily goal, a live order feed, a roast queue and a fulfilment board you drag orders across; Pelago, a ten-page sales console for a ceramics studio, with demand by category month by month against last year, a 24-hour order dial, a packing bench you drag orders across and kiln firings; Pembra, a nine-section people, rota and payroll app for a two-hotel group, with a live shift pulse, a drag-and-drop rota, timesheets, time off, hiring and a monthly pay run; Kelvo, a nine-page people, rota and payroll app for three climbing gyms, with an hourly coverage strip on a drag-and-drop rota, suggested cover for open shifts, timesheets, time off, hiring and a pay run that stamps PAID; Folka, a ten-section people, rota and payroll app for a coffee company, with a colour-block overview, a drag-and-drop rota with an hourly coverage row, staff photos, time off, hiring and a monthly pay run; Selvar, a ten-section sales dashboard and CRM for a solar company, with a quarter-to-quota runway, a drag-and-drop deal board, a forecast you adjust deal by deal, lead scoring and a rule-based Copilot; Petalo, a florist's point of sale and back office, with a working register, an order board you drag across, stock with vase life, a staff rota and tills you count and close; Olvara, a twelve-page back office for a skincare brand, with a product shelf by collection, a courier pickup countdown, a lab board you drag batches into stock, a cure schedule, orders and returns, stockists and a team rota; Ondra, an eight-section marketing and sales desk for an outdoor gear brand, with a performance chart you switch by its headline figures, a campaign calendar you drag to reschedule, budgets, a wholesale pipeline you drag to Won and channel, funnel and attribution reports; Ambrel, an eleven-section point of sale and back office for a homewares shop, with a register where a product flies into a till-roll ticket, members with tiers and points, a printed receipt, refunds by line, a cash-drawer count, deposits, stock with reorders and closed-day reports; Tessly, a thirteen-section sales CRM for a stone and tile studio, with client files and a touchpoint timeline, a pipeline ladder, a deal board you drag to Won, a quarter forecast, projects, invoices and commissions; Solvik, an eight-section sales CRM in frosted glass for a solar installer, with a drag-and-drop deal board tinted by stage, customer profiles, a schedule, invoices that stamp PAID and growth reports; Kerfa, a ten-section sales dashboard in frosted glass for a furniture workshop, with revenue against last year that morphs by range and channel, a deal board where Won books a real order, a quote builder, orders with deposits, accounts and quotas; Moorly, a ten-section broker portal for a marine insurer in frosted glass, with application stages drawn as a sea route a boat sails along, a quote builder, a pipeline board you drag, renewals, book rolls, policies with endorsements and certificates, and agency bills; Wynlo, a twenty-page sales CRM for a brand selling online, on marketplaces and to shops, with a deal board you drag, a forecast, a country map and about 2,000 orders with a refunds queue; Merrin, a twelve-page sales CRM for a home-goods studio, with a sales chart you switch by headline figure, a deal board you drag, orders packed in bulk and a photo catalogue with stock; Pacely, a ten-page physiotherapy clinic app with a clinic floor you drag visits across, recovery charts, a rehab-phase board, an exercise library, outcomes and insurance claims; Fitlo, the admin dashboard of a clothing shop, with orders and returns, stock by size, discounts, banners and fit insights from its size advisor, shipped with the storefront it runs; SOLUM, a store admin dashboard for orders, products and customers that ships with the storefront it runs; Cirrel, a thirteen-page shop admin in iOS-style liquid glass, with orders packed on a board you drag, stock, invoices, discounts and one inbox for site chat, Instagram and texts; Sorvo, a nine-page creator studio for a video channel in frosted glass, with a retention curve you scrub, an upload planner you drag across the week, a brand-deals board and a merch shop; Lumelle, an eleven-page shop admin in frosted glass for a candle maker that sells online, in its own shop and wholesale, with sales stacked by channel, a working till, a catalogue that re-sorts in place and a wholesale board you drag; and Rotela, an eleven-section HR and staff-rota app for a three-hotel group, with a staffing curve by department, a week rota you drag shifts across, leave, the pay run, a hiring board and onboarding; Tidra, a crew HR app for a ferry line, with the day’s sailings on one timeline, short-crewed departures you fix by calling someone in, a roster you drag watches across, time off, the pay run and hiring; Levra, an eight-section sales app for a four-shop bakery, with a race of today’s takings against last week, collect orders, a cake board you drag, the wholesale round, a bake plan, stamp cards and refunds that come off the takings; Arpeo, a nine-section front desk for a music school, with tuition by format that morphs between months and weeks, a room planner you drag lessons across, teachers' pay runs, students' practice and exam readiness, enrolments and recitals; Bastio, a fifteen-page identity-check and fraud desk for a holiday-rental marketplace, where checks rise above a line and hang below it day by day, a decision is stamped and the next check slides in, cases drag across a board and a rule's threshold drags while its would-catch count re-counts; Ostrel, a nineteen-view web and shop analytics app for a record store on pale cobalt, where web visits rise above a line and people through the shop doors hang below it and morph between ranges, a sources table re-sorts as its rows glide, web orders move on from picking to shipped and restock orders land in stock; Caelo, an eighteen-view flight desk for a private jet charter operator in charcoal and gold, where every jet in the air flies its arc over a dotted world map that glides between the world and Europe, legs drag along a fleet timeline with clash checks and Undo, a trip is priced across every cabin size and an overdue invoice is marked paid; Dovell, a twenty-one-view job desk for a kitchen fitter in sage and pine green, where a five-arc stage ring fills as you tick each checklist, job cards drag across six columns and raise their invoices, and crew visits drag between days on the site plan; Nousa, a twenty-view ideas desk for a pottery studio on warm paper and cobalt, where idea cards drag from Spark to Launched and book a kiln trial, Muse drafts three ideas onto the board with a simple rule-based generator, and firings drag across the kiln plan; Tallo, a twenty-two-view work planner for a podcast studio in sea-glass and teal, where tasks drag from a tray onto the day’s timeline and the blocks after them slide later, Fit the rest drops the others into the free gaps, and cards drag across the task board; Scenra, a twenty-two-view production desk for a repertory theatre on true neutral and cobalt, where calls drag along the run sheet and push the calls that wait on them, two shows booked into one room flag a clash, and the timeline zooms from the day to the week and the season; Wardel, a thirty-view account-security desk for a bike workshop on saffron paper with an ink sidebar, where every sign-in is a bead on a 24-hour clock you scrub across fourteen days, a posture gauge refills as you fix things and ID checks show their liveness and face-match rings; Musela, an eleven-page visitor desk for a museum on olive-grey with a stone-olive sidebar, where a dot for every three visitors walks between rooms on a live floor plan you can replay through the day; Levena, a ten-section people and rota app for a bakery group on true-neutral grey with a saffron icon rail, where every shop's cover strip counts heads on the floor against heads needed hour by hour as you drag shifts along the day or onto someone; Vernly, a ten-page work desk for a six-person translation studio on a true-neutral page with a sand sidebar and a mustard accent, where every work session is a block you drag across the week planner, a studio timer logs the hours and invoices are stamped paid; Mendo, a nine-page care desk for a small-animal vet clinic in black and white, where every dose, drip and meal on the ward round is a chip you tick or drag to another time, beside a four-room diary you drag visits across; Amplo, a ten-page campaign and ad-budget desk for an indie record label on graphite with a cobalt accent, where the ad wallet sits beside a spinning vinyl record whose ring is the live budget by channel and slides to the new split when you rebalance, with a stage board you drag campaigns across and a flight plan whose bars you drag and stretch; Fragio, a nine-page growing desk for a glasshouse fruit farm on warm paper with a persimmon accent, where each glasshouse is a row of season phases you drag a week later and the phases after it follow, beside live climate for every house, picking crews and invoices stamped paid; Gustra, an eleven-page operations desk for a 48-turbine offshore wind farm on a true-neutral page with a marigold accent, where every rotor turns on a live farm map whose colours ripple downwind as you switch between output, status, health and wind, with a grid cap you drag to hold the farm back, a work-order board you drag and a vessel day you drag trips along; collections.name: SaaS & analytics dashboards
collections.tagline: An AI platform console, live commerce analytics, a marketing board and a fitness tracker.
collections.intro: Thirty-six dashboards for a software product: Orrery, a ten-screen console for an AI API platform with a streaming playground, request traces, keys and billing; Prism, a single-screen live analytics wall for an online store; Kestrel, an eleven-page marketing dashboard; Stride, a seven-page personal fitness tracker with a workout log that moves every page; Halsa, an eleven-page personal health record where vitals, doses, lab results and appointments live in one place; Kairo, a six-page revenue analytics app for a subscription business, where picking a metric morphs the whole report and a deal is dragged into Won; Murmura, an eleven-page social media manager for agencies with role-based access, a composer with live previews for eight networks, approvals, a unified inbox and analytics; Vitrea, a nine-page App Store publishing desk for an iOS studio in liquid glass, with a release board you drag from build to live, a review inbox, subscriber cohorts, product-page tests and payouts; Halvo, an eleven-page smart-home app in frosted glass over a photo of each room, with a climate dial you drag, lights you dim and recolour, energy charts that morph, cameras, scenes, music and family access; Calda, an eleven-page smart-home app in smoked grey glass with one sky-blue accent, with a climate dial you drag, doors you slide to lock, energy bars that morph, a weekly heating schedule, cameras, scenes and a highlight colour you pick; Nestra, an eleven-page smart-home app for one house in frosted day and night glass, with a thermostat ring you drag, a week plan you paint, energy in kWh or cost, cameras, locks and a PIN alarm, scenes and a sidebar that folds to an icon rail; Hemli, an eleven-page smart-home app in frosted glass over a blurred living room, with an Ask bar that understands typed commands, a floor plan whose lamps each throw their own pool of light, a heat dial you turn, an alarm ring that counts down, scenes, music and guest door codes; Kovara, a ten-section smart-home app for a family house with a live floor plan whose rooms glow as you switch the lamps on it, a thermostat you drag like a tape, a week plan you paint, energy against the hourly price with cheap-hour car charging, cameras and a PIN alarm; Nooka, an eleven-section smart-home app for a household with two homes, with a ring of ticks you drag to set the heating, a floor plan with lights, warmth and people layers, a week plan you paint, cameras, door codes and energy with bills; Embra, an eleven-section host desk for six holiday cabins, with a warm-up planner whose heating points you drag while the time each cabin is warm moves with them, a heating dial, devices with hot tubs and a sauna, energy with bills, cameras and door codes, and a booking calendar you drag stays across; Nimbra, a fifteen-page revenue analytics app for a SaaS company in frosted navy glass, with recurring revenue by plan that switches to new or churned, funnels drawn as glass steps by channel, a retention heatmap, rule-based insights and a campaign board you drag; Calvio, a sixteen-view revenue analytics app for a vet-clinic software company, whose MRR bridge builds from start through new, expansion, contraction and churn to now and morphs between 30 days, a quarter and a year, with accounts you upgrade in a drawer, segments that count live and automations whose steps light up one by one; Milvo, a nineteen-view training and club app for a running club on green-grey and lime, where a twelve-week half-marathon plan is drawn as a running track with every friend on it, sessions drag between days on the week grid and the leaderboard’s podium rises and re-sorts; and Kelpo, a nineteen-view social media desk for a surf school on warm paper and berry rose, where every channel's reach stacks as a river that morphs between metrics and ranges and folds a channel out when you tap it, posts drag across a week calendar, saved replies send from a two-pane inbox and creators drag from pitched to agreed; Plotta, a fifteen-page reporting desk for a subscription business in olive-black and lime, with a report library of live chart previews, schedules and exports, funnels, cohorts and a rule-based Ask Plotta that drafts a report from a typed question; Cairnly, an eleven-page personal system for habits, study and money in graphite and marigold, where every habit you tick drops a stone onto the day's cairn; Tolvi, a twelve-page pet-health app for a home with two dogs and a cat on a sage-white page with a mint sidebar and an emerald accent, where each pet's day is a strip of sleep, walks, play and meals under a heart line that zooms and reads out any minute, and switching pet morphs every chart; Halvi, a nine-page personal health app with a live heart rate, a health-score dial, visits you book and move, a week schedule you drag and doses you tick off; Brisko, a ten-page workflow-automation app where you build scenarios on a canvas, run one and watch each step light, retry failed runs and see a month-end forecast of operations; Ombria, a ten-page smart-home app in grey frosted glass, where a thermostat dial is dragged, a heating week is painted hour by hour, locks snap shut and the sidebar folds to an icon rail; Zephra, a ten-page weather app in slate glass and sky blue, where a rain radar is scrubbed or played from three hours ago to six ahead, every forecast reads that same rain field, and an activity planner scores each hour of the week; Lullo, a ten-page music-listening app in pastel clay, where a record spins up when you press play and a player dock counts every song you finish; Audora, an eight-page podcast audience-analytics app, where plays are counted as they arrive and episodes are dragged across a release calendar; Hovira, a nine-page smart-home app in tinted glass over a photo of the room it controls, with an AC dial dragged along a cold-to-hot arc, blinds you drag shut, energy that morphs, security you arm, plain commands in Ask Hovira and an Appearance panel that restyles it live; Vivra, a nine-page personal health monitor in frosted glass over a photo of a room, where a Room light slider dims the room behind the glass, with heart, activity and sleep with its stages, watch faces whose dial sets the mood colour, habits, medication and a journal, and an Appearance panel that restyles it live; Tutelo, an eight-page language-lessons dashboard where you pick a teacher, book one of their free days and watch a progress ring fill tick by tick, with courses, tutors, messages, a week calendar, a streak and an Appearance panel that restyles it live; Lumio, a five-page smart-home app with nineteen sub-pages in dark glass over a photo of the room, with a thermostat ring you drag, energy bars that switch between week, month and year, lights you dim, doors you slide to unlock, scenes, bills against a budget and an Appearance panel that restyles it live; Havena, an eight-page smart-home app in warm frosted glass over a photo of each room, with device tiles you slide on and off, a lighting ring and a thermostat dial you drag, a room dock, energy for every day of the month with bills you pay, scenes, cameras and locks, and an Appearance panel that restyles it live; Curava, a ten-page patient-care app in navy and seafoam with a curved rail whose bubble travels from page to page, where a visit is booked in four steps with Undo, the heart-rate chart morphs between 7, 30 and 90 days and today's medicines tick off, with vitals and lab results, a pharmacy with checkout, video visits, an inbox and an Appearance panel that restyles it live; Carevo, a six-page patient health dashboard in forest and lime with a booking column on every page, where a doctor is booked on a calendar of free, full and off days, the heart rate flows as a live wave, a weight dial is dragged to log today and the vitals morph between 7 days and a year, with medicines and refill warnings, lab results on their ranges and an Appearance panel that restyles it live; and Radiva, an eight-page patient imaging-results portal in mint and charcoal with a nav capsule whose light disc hangs from the active page, where the radiologist's note is read in plain words, two scans are compared by dragging a divider across them, a scan is booked at a nearby imaging centre in four steps and the visit's prep checklist is ticked off, with sharing by doctor, a body guide, a glossary, a care chat and an Appearance panel that restyles it live. Plain HTML and CSS with JavaScript or TypeScript (Stride with no dependencies, the others with GSAP; Halvo, Nestra, Kovara, Nooka, Nimbra, Calvio, Milvo, Kelpo, Plotta, Cairnly, Tolvi, Halvi, Brisko, Ombria, Zephra, Lullo, Audora, Hovira, Vivra, Tutelo, Lumio, Havena, Curava, Carevo and Radiva are React and TypeScript), ready to wire to your own data.

collections.name: Finance dashboards
collections.tagline: Money on screen — a trading terminal, a finance tracker, a portfolio and invoicing.
collections.intro: Every dashboard about money: Fathom, a live trading terminal with eight pages; Rivet, a nine-page personal finance app in black and neon with a light theme, cards you freeze and cap, a ledger with bank sync, a 30-day forecast, budgets, goals and a portfolio with buy and sell; Meridian, a portfolio that moves like a single instrument; Coffer, eight pages of invoicing and accounting where recording a payment stamps the invoice PAID; Rivolo, an eleven-page money app for freelancers with every pot on one bar, safe-to-spend shown as its sum, a two-sided money-flow chart and a tax set-aside on every client payment; Kesta, a ten-page production-finance app for a film studio with a cash-bridge waterfall, four currency wallets and budgets per production; Tillo, a ten-page money app for a bike shop with a cash-flow chart you drag across to total any run of months, a three-step send flow and cards that frost and turn over; Kofra, an eleven-page business bank account for a ceramics studio with a balance runway that forecasts 30 days, invoices that stamp PAID and feed a tax jar, and a hold-to-send payment flow; Sovra, an eleven-page business bank account for a florist with a cash-flow chart you drag across to total any stretch, team cards that frost when frozen and a VAT return worked out against its pot; Kinby, a ten-page family money app with a swipe-carousel wallet of everyone's cards, kids' cards on weekly limits, a bills calendar with paydays and goals that fill as jars; Obolo, a thirteen-page business-finance app for an olive-oil exporter with four currency wallets, a money in and out chart, a live converter and invoices that stamp PAID; Grista, an eleven-page business bank account for a three-shop bakery with its cash drawn day by day, the big days pinned and a year you drag through, team cards that lock with a padlock and a what-if cash forecast; Orvel, a twelve-page finance console for a vinyl pressing plant with every payment drawn as a dot you brush to filter the ledger, a review queue dealt as a stack, invoices that stamp PAID and bills that take two sign-offs; Corvane, an eleven-section payments operations portal for a card processor with a threshold lab you drag across last month's risk scores, a review queue for held payments, a disputes board, payouts and an audit log of every action; Rivlet, a twenty-five-page finance and HR back office for three climbing gyms with a sort desk you drag card charges into their categories on, cash across four accounts, cards that freeze, a profit and loss statement and tax filings that pay from the reserve; Kinlo, an eleven-section finance and HR back office for a two-site cinema with takings by tickets, bar and hire that morph between ranges, card payments filed in bulk, invoices that stamp PAID, a VAT return and a pay run you approve and pay; Coffra, a twenty-four-page finance and people back office for three climbing gyms with a cash-flow chart that morphs between ranges and gyms, a month-end close that ticks itself, transactions filed by suggestion, cards that frost when frozen and a pay run you approve; Ledra, an eight-section money, people and paperwork back office for a landscape architecture studio with a cash chart whose three-month forecast four what-if switches reshape, card charges you drag into their categories, invoices that stamp PAID, bills you approve and pay and a four-step pay run; Covry, an eleven-section money and people back office for a group of veterinary clinics in frosted glass, with a cash chart that morphs between months, weeks and one clinic, card payments you file from a stack with always-file rules, invoices that stamp PAID, a pay run you approve and contracts signed on a drawn pad; Talvo, a thirteen-page business-finance app for a craft brewery with a 90-day cash forecast you drag bills and invoices across, bills that stamp PAID and a treasury ladder; Tilvo, a nine-page money app for an independent record label with a cash planner you drag payments across while the balance re-draws, cards that frost when frozen, a royalty run you approve, invoices that stamp PAID and a report builder; Ferna, a ten-page money app for a freelance photographer, with cash flow and a forecast, a tax reserve that fills itself from every client payment, pots whose rings fill, cards that frost when frozen and invoices that stamp PAID; and Kestro, an eleven-section on-chain trading desk with a live candle chart that morphs between timeframes, an order ticket that waits for its block, a screener that re-sorts, swap with its route, pools and vaults; Ardena, an eighteen-view property investor app in smoked glass, where the portfolio value morphs between ranges, late rent is reminded or marked received, loans get an overpayment planner and offers on homes move along a five-step track into the portfolio; Zesto, a twenty-four-view family money app on near-black with a lime-to-cyan gradient, where the last 30 days stack by category and morph between the family and each person, cards flip and frost when frozen, budgets and goal jars fill, and a chores board you drag across pays the bonus; Settla, a twenty-one-view payments desk for an animation studio on pale olive and chartreuse, where automatic runs drag to another day on the month's runway while the balance line re-forecasts above a floor, approvals fly out and an invoice is marked paid with a stamp; Brindo, a twenty-six-view spend management desk for a film and TV company on warm paper and terracotta, where the team’s company cards fan out to pick, freeze and re-limit, approvals fly out of the queue and receipt slips file onto their payment; Cofra, an eleven-page personal money app for a freelancer in black and white, where the month's budget is a shelf of glass jars you drag coins between and the cards sit in a pile you flick through and freeze under frost; Penvo, a ten-section business banking app for a bakery on a calm neutral page with an icon rail and a cobalt accent, where a cash runway pins every bill, standing order and the pay run on the day it leaves, switching unapproved bills in or out redraws the forecast, team cards frost when frozen and a bills board is approved and stamped paid; Pursa, a nine-page personal money app for a freelancer in black and white with one orange highlight, where a cash runway pins every bill, save and payday on the line and marks the lowest point ahead; Saffra, a twelve-page personal and studio money app for a freelance photographer, where a money river follows every euro from income through needs, wants, studio and future to what it was spent on; Verdelo, a nine-page household money app in smoked glass with a mint glow, where a wallet of glass cards is thrown aside and flipped, the balance carries on as a dashed forecast to the month's end and savings pots fill as glass tubes; Oasel, an eleven-page loan desk for a private lender in sand glass, where three sliders stress-test each loan live against its loan-to-value gauge and debt-cover bar, applications drag onto Fund and a recorded payment stamps PAID; Tolva, a ten-page autopay console for a craft brewery on a moss-green ground, where each payment rule is edited on one black card (a calendar for the day, the plan and amount, the accounts as bars to pay from), every rule is a card you switch on or off, and bills are approved in bulk; Tendly, an eleven-page no-spend challenge app in forest green and cream, where the month fills in as thirty days, a one-tap check-in grows the streak and an urge on the 72-hour waiting list is let go as money kept; Verdin, an eight-page personal banking app in deep green, lime and sky, where six months of cash flow show money in above the line and money out below it, cards shuffle in a stack and freeze under frost, and money is sent with a review step and Undo; and Banqo, a seven-page personal-banking app that puts four banks in one view, where a rail of bank marks refocuses every figure, the card deck deals its front card to the back, money is sent in three steps with Undo and moved between your own banks, with statistics, card freezes and limits, subscriptions, scheduled transfers, requests and an Appearance panel that restyles it live. Calm, transform-only motion, ready for your own numbers.

collections.name: Dashboard starter
collections.tagline: Two dashboards to start with — a portfolio and a finance tracker.
collections.intro: Two money dashboards together: Meridian, a one-screen portfolio that moves like a single instrument, in plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript, and Rivet, a nine-page personal finance app in black and neon with a light theme, built with TypeScript. Both are ready to wire to your own data.

collections.name: Product landing pages
collections.tagline: One-page sites that sell a single thing beautifully.
collections.intro: Scroll-driven one-page sites for a product or a studio: fresh mangoes, dark chocolate, sneakers, headphones, an architecture coverflow, a synthwave gallery, a quiet audio brand, an architecture studio, a car-rental page where the hero car is the control, a real-estate agency page whose hero film plays as you scroll, a homebuying page with a working cash-back calculator and an art marketplace whose wall of art fans out and folds into a portrait wall, plus a one-screen glass hero for a lighting shop whose lamps switch on as you brush past them. Rebrand one, launch it.

collections.name: Games & playful pages
collections.tagline: A shooting range, a deadline that chases you, a studio intro.
collections.intro: Three one-pagers built to be played with: a neon shooting range where you hit to level up, a deadline timer that comes for you, and a studio intro for websites, apps and stores.

collections.name: Love & celebrations
collections.tagline: Little animated gifts — birthdays, anniversaries, a love letter.
collections.intro: Pages made to be sent to someone: a pixel-art love letter, a birthday film, candles to blow out, a long-distance date, a heart built from a thousand "i love you"s. Personal, playful and easy to make your own.

collections.name: 404 pages
collections.tagline: Lost pages that make people smile instead of leave.
collections.intro: Not-found pages that keep visitors around: a magnifying glass on your cursor, weather that leaks into the room, an astronaut adrift. One of them is free.

collections.name: Every button
collections.tagline: Every button in the store — delete, send, share, download, upload and toggles.
collections.intro: The complete button set: the delete buttons, the send and share buttons, the download and upload buttons, and the buttons and toggles — every one in the store, in one download, at the biggest saving.

collections.name: Buttons & toggles
collections.tagline: Toggles that fill, stars that mint, buttons that grow into controls.
collections.intro: Everyday controls with a flourish: a toggle that fills instead of lighting up, a theme toggle the new light floods out of, a favourite button that mints its own star, buttons whose label is the moving part, a liquid hover, and soft-UI buttons that grow into their own controls.

collections.name: Download & upload buttons
collections.tagline: Progress you can watch — liquid fills, unrolling rings, a parachute.
collections.intro: Buttons that turn waiting into something to watch: the outline becomes the progress bar, the arrow becomes the water, a glass fills, a parachute drops the file. Download, upload and submit — each one shows its progress in a different way.

collections.name: Send & share buttons
collections.tagline: Send, subscribe, share, publish — each with a flourish.
collections.intro: The buttons people press to reach someone: a send that folds into a paper plane, a subscribe that flies off, a share that fans into channels, a publish that rolls its own weather, a contact button that reacts when poked.

collections.name: Delete buttons
collections.tagline: Buttons that make deleting feel final — and fun.
collections.intro: Delete, but memorable: the bin eats the label, the paper crumples and flies, the button dissolves what it swallows. Each one confirms the action without a single extra dialog.

collections.name: Cart & checkout
collections.tagline: Add-to-cart, pay and checkout moments that sell.
collections.intro: The moments that close a sale: an item that hops into a cart that comes for it, a pay button that looks at you, a card that swipes through, a checkout where the card is the form — plus two shop pages to put them in.

collections.name: Navigation bars
collections.tagline: Tab bars and docks that stretch, glow and flow.
collections.intro: Bottom navs, tab bars and docks where the indicator is the show: a drop of liquid, an electric arc, a filament of light, a word that becomes the dock.

collections.name: OTP & verification codes
collections.tagline: One-time code fields that make verifying a moment.
collections.intro: Verification codes with a twist: digits dealt as cards, a code pressed into obsidian, a safe that dials open, a key that gets cut, a field that seals itself, and frosted glass boxes that flip to mint.

collections.name: Mobile app interactions
collections.tagline: Chat, swipes and onboarding that feel native.
collections.intro: The moments a mobile app is judged by: messages delivered by tube, a composer whose tray swings out, an iOS list row that shreds, and a crypto wallet onboarding in one continuous shot.

collections.name: Inputs & feedback
collections.tagline: Sliders, ratings, search and uploads people enjoy using.
collections.intro: Input and feedback controls with personality: a spice slider whose pepper catches fire, a loudness slider, a rating face that feels it, a search icon that opens into the field, a file upload you can actually ship, and a loader where the last bead jumps to the front.

collections.name: Playful scenes
collections.tagline: Little worlds to play with — a dragon egg, a snow globe, four seasons.
collections.intro: Interactive scenes that make a page memorable: hatch a dragon, shake a snow globe, turn one tree through four seasons, tap a day to change the sky, wake a lamp, steer a reptile cursor, and read the time off a brass spider.

collections.name: Cards & sections
collections.tagline: Team, product and feature sections that move.
collections.intro: Three page sections: a team grid with one person in colour at a time, a cola card that unfolds when you tap the can, and a product card for sound, elevated.
